A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SMART-R1, with matching main sections and Appendices A.1–A.3. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SMART-R1 experiments, ablations and simulation rollouts in Tables 1–7 and Figures 4–7, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original SMART-R1 experiments, ablations and simulation rollouts in Tables 1–7 and Figures 4–7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same architecture, CAT-K supervision, MPO objective and SFT–RFT–SFT procedure. Adding the parenthetical label 'R1-style' does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use WOMD and the 2025 WOSAC traffic-simulation task. The intersection and U-turn scenarios in Section 4.4 and Appendix A.3 are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2, 4 and 7, including PPO, DPO and GRPO against MPO. TrajTok's citation changes from Zhang et al. (2025b) to Zhang et al. (2026), while its comparison entries remain identical.

E3.justification: Both retain the same data splits, 32 eight-second simulated futures, 2025 WOSAC metrics, 7M-parameter model and training schedule. Ablations still use the same 2% validation subset.

E4.justification: Tables 3–6 retain the training-stage, policy-optimization, reward-threshold and KL-regularization ablations. The qualitative case studies in Figures 4–7 and their accompanying analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Results remain point estimates under the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and qualitative findings in Figures 4–7 are unchanged. Both report SMART-R1's Realism Meta score of 0.7858 and minADE of 1.2885, with the same rankings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–6 are unchanged, as are the metric definitions in Appendix A.1. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty claims for SMART-R1 and MPO, the SFT–RFT–SFT contribution, and the first-place WOSAC claim.

C2.justification: Explanations concerning distribution recovery, catastrophic forgetting, policy optimization and hyperparameter effects are unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the same interpretations of TrajTok and comBOT; no substantive limitations are added.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 retains 64-epoch pretraining, two 16-epoch SFT phases, alpha = 0.77 and beta = 0.04. Implementation disclosures and references to supplementary simulation videos are unchanged, with no new code, hardware or runtime information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Peng et al. (2024), DriveX, UniSplat and Plan-R1. These modestly broaden the cited literature without revising the central positioning or novelty argument; existing TrajTok and Reason-RFT references also receive publication updates.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments, changes the header from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', clarifies the 'R1-style' label and updates citations and bibliographic wording. The scientific exposition and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgments block and expanded bibliography reflow the reference pages and shift the appendix start from page 12 to page 13. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–7 retain their organization and substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: The added citations slightly broaden the bibliography, while acknowledgments and publication updates improve documentary completeness. These are limited editorial changes: the substantive explanations, reproducibility information and evidence in Tables 1–7 and Appendix A remain unchanged, leaving overall paper quality essentially the same.
